title: SC22297 - Colemans Kitchen Woods Chilmington
description:
Kent County Council are looking for a supplier to create surfaced access points into Colemans Kitchen Wood and neighbouring field. By doing this we hope to increase number of people into the woods which will align with Ashford Borough Councils plans to promote the local wildlife.

Another requirement of the project is to provide a full surfaced route suitable for all users from Colemans Kitchen Wood to Chilmington Green Lane which will ensure residents and future residents have a safe route to access the woods and the Environmental Centre. The works align with Ashford Borough Councils strategic development for the Chilmington Development as Ashford Borough Council plan to build parks and play areas around the woods so by improving access to the woods it will make it easier and more appealing for residents to access.

One key part of the specification is replacing the existing stiles with metal gates to make the paths accessible for wheelchair users and those who are less mobile. These gates will be supplied by Kent County Council and will be opening two ways so that people coming from both directions will be able to push the gate open. We have also asked for improved signage in the area so people are aware they are using the Public Right of Way Network and can see the impact Kent County Council is having on the local community. This will also be helpful as people can look up the local footpath network and start to plan either leisure activities or commuting to the local school based on this network.

title: SC23077 - Bridleway AW244 Chilmington
description:
As part of Chilmington Development Project Ashford Borough Council want to use the existing \r
PROW network especially Public Bridleway AW244 area to improve resident access to the \r
countryside, the local school and other areas of the development. The works will make the paths \r
suitable for disabled users and fit in with the plans for making the woods and surrounding area \r
accessible by bicycle as well.\r
\r
The requirement of this project is the creation of a surfaced bridleway leading from Ashford Road, Great Chart to Bucksford Lane, providing opportunities for people to use the bridleway to connect to the Great Chart village in one direction or get to Sevington Environmental Centre and our previous work in Coleman Kitchen Wood in the other direction. By doing this we hope to increase numbers into the local environment, increasing residents time spent outside promoting \r
green/healthy and active lifestyles. The works align with Ashford Borough Councils strategic \r
development for the Chilmington Development.\r
\r
The work expected to be carried out by the successful contractor would be the excavation of the \r
existing ground to install a 2.5-metre-wide type 1 surfaced bridleway with timber edging. Due to \r
the width available we will also be leaving a grass strip to the side of the path, so Equestrians \r
Horse users have the option to use the surfaced route or the grass route. The contractor will also \r
be required to replace a field gate on the path as the current field gate is redundant.

title: Provision of support for SMI/CCMI Physical Health Checks and Flu Vaccinations (Ashford Place)
description:
A variation to extend the existing contractual arrangements within Ashford Place was granted for a further period of 7 (seven) months. With effect from 1st August 2022 the contract expiry date will therefore change from 31st August 2022 to 31st March 2023. This is an extension to the SMI/CCMI health checks with the inclusion of Flu vaccinations.

Scope of service: Severe Mental Illness and Common Complex Mental Illness Physical Health and Flu Vaccinations. 

Ashford Place will provide a peer support service that will support adults with lived experience of severe mental illness in the borough, including people from local BAME communities to access and receive a full annual physical health assessment and appropriate follow-up care.

The service will support with:
• Reducing inequality of health access and health outcome for SMI patients;
• Reducing excess morbidity and mortality rates for SMI patients;
• Reducing reliance on non-elective care for preventable acute physical conditions; and
• Increasing take up of flu vaccinations for individuals with severe mental illness.

title: Call for Competition - St Pancras Enhancement Project RIBA 2 Design and Operational Concept Feasibility Study
description:
HS1 Ltd has the 30-year concession to own, operate and maintain High Speed 1 (HS1), the UK's only high-speed railway, as well as the stations along the route: St Pancras International, Stratford International, Ebbsfleet International and Ashford International.

International rail services are currently provided by Eurostar who have expressed an aspiration to grow their passenger volumes from 19m today to 30m by 2030 across their network. To support these growth aspirations, HS1 has commissioned an initial feasibility study to explore a) the likely future passenger numbers that will need to be accommodated in the international part of St Pancras station and b) the required spatial and operational changes that will be necessary to unlock the required capacity.

This initial work has identified that expansion is feasible. HS1 is now ready to progress to design and operational concept feasibility stage (RIBA2) to design, deliver and operationalise a reconfigured ground floor operation of the International Zone delivering a significant uplift in passenger capacity that meets forecast requirements until at least 2035 and potentially 2040.

This is a Call for Competition using the Negotiated Procurement Procedure.  Therefore, for this stage the following documents are attached:

Local authorities have a legal obligation to support the work of Coroner's, to fund all the costs of the service and to provide the necessary resources to enable them to carry out their statutory obligations under the Coroners and Justice Act 2009. This includes the provision of appropriate contractual arrangements for the removal of the deceased. For the four Kent coroner areas of Mid Kent & Medway, North-West Kent, North-East Kent and Central & South-East Kent, KCC is the lead authority for the administrative areas of Kent and Medway.

There are two requirements for this service: 
Lot 1 - Coroner Removals Service and Lot 2 - Coroner Transfers Service. 

The Coroners Removals Service (Lot 1) has been separated into 15 contract areas:
1 (A) - Sevenoaks A (above A25)
1 (B) - Sevenoaks B (below A25)
1 (C) - Dartford & Gravesham 
1 (D) - Tunbridge Wells 
1 (E) - Tonbridge and Malling 
1 (F) - Medway  
1 (G) - Maidstone 
1 (H) - West Swale 
1 (I) - East Swale 
1 (J) - Ashford  
1 (K) - Canterbury  
1 (L) - Shepway
1 (M) - Thanet 
1 (N) - Dover NEK

The Coroners Removals Service includes the provision of appropriate contractual arrangements for the removal of the deceased to a designated mortuary. The movement of the deceased to the mortuary constitutes a "Coroners Removal".

Where an organisation is awarded a contract area, they are responsible for providing this service throughout the specified area. They must deliver this service 24/7, 365 days a year, and in accordance with the service requirements as detailed within the specification.

The Coroners Transfers Service (Lot 2) has been separated into 2 contract areas:
2 (A) West Kent Transfers
2 (B) East Kent Transfers

In certain circumstances, it is necessary to transfer the deceased from a designated mortuary to another designated mortuary. These transfers can occur locally as a transfer between mortuaries within Kent and Medway but can occur outside of Kent. 

Where an organisation is awarded a contract area, they are responsible for providing this service throughout the specified area. They must deliver this service 24/7, 365 days a year, and in accordance with the service requirements as detailed within the specification.

title: Sanctuary SAFER Scheme
description:
Kent County Council are looking to commission a suitably qualified Provider to deliver the Property Security element of the Sanctuary Access for Eligible Residents SAFER Scheme. The SAFER Scheme is a new preventative service which will enable victims and survivors of domestic abuse to remain in their own home, where it is safe to do so and where the perpetrator does not live.\r
\r
The SAFER Scheme aims to improve safety, improve health, wellbeing, and prevent harm.\r
\r
The vision for the service is to provide and install approved property security measures to survivors of domestic abuse, adults and children, once the property has been adapted the household will be defined as residing in safe accommodation and will be in line with the new statutory duties introduced by the Domestic Abuse Act 2021. \r
\r
KCC are looking to commission  a property security Provider to undertake countywide property assessments, provide and install approved property security measures across the county, to improve safety and to aid in delaying a perpetrator gaining access to the property of the victim or survivor. This will lead to further positive outcomes such as, improved access to support for underserved groups, a reduction in victim risk level, repeat offences, homelessness, and the need for emergency accommodation.\r
\r
The Provider will need to demonstrate that they are cognisant of survivors needs, and able to conduct property assessments, provide and install the relevant property security measures. \r
\r
The service will be delivered countywide by a single Provider, with the option to subcontract specific works to secondary providers pre vetted by the Provider where necessary.\r
\r
The Provider will hold the contract with KCC and be ultimately responsible for the delivery of the service through the implementation and development of a responsive service that is engaged with partner agencies.\r
\r
The SAFER Scheme will be delivered through one lot, and Countywide delivery includes the following Kent local authority areas, Ashford, Canterbury, Dartford, Dover, Gravesham, Folkestone and Hythe, Maidstone, Sevenoaks, Swale, Thanet, Tonbridge and Malling, Tunbridge Wells. \r
\r
The Provider must be able to travel countywide in a timely manner.\r
\r
The contract is anticipated to commence on 1 December 2023 and will run for a period of two years, expiring 30 November 2025 with the option for two one year extensions at the discretion of the Council, unless terminated in accordance with the published Conditions of Contract.\r
\r
SQ submissions are due via the Kent Business Portal by 12pm on 31 May 2023. Please allow adequate time for uploading documents and submit responses well in advance of the closing time to avoid last minute problems.\r
\r
Interested parties are also asked to direct any questions via the Portal.

title: Provision of a Community of Interest Network (CoIN) to Surrey Heartlands Integrated Care Board (ICB)
description:
NHS Surrey Heartlands Integrated Care Board (ICB) (the Commissioner) has awarded a contract for the provision of a Community of Interest Network (CoIN) to British Telecommunications PLC. 

The CoIN provides resilient network connectivity for most healthcare providers in Surrey including, Royal Surrey, Ashford and St Peters, Surrey and Borders Partnership (SABP), Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trusts, and Surrey and Sussex Hospitals NHS Trust, and serves approx. 210 individual sites across the geography.
The CoIN, along with other regional CoINs, connects to the national Health and Social Care Network (HSCN) and provides a sophisticated perimeter security solution and cybersecurity protection, over and above what individual local sites have. 
The procurement followed the Direct Award process as set out in the buyer's guide of the Crown Commercial Services Network Services 2 Framework, RM3808. 

The contract has been awarded under Lot 1 - Data Access which covers inter-site connectivity services, enabling site-to-site or site-to-cloud/internet interconnectivity, including but not limited to:
•	Wide Area Network (WAN)
•	Fibre and other connectivity solutions
•	Network equipment (such as switches and routers). 

The contract commenced on 10th July 2023 and has been awarded for a term of 5 years. 

The estimated annual contract value is £1,202,229.12 ex. VAT and the estimated total contract value is £6,011,145.62 ex. VAT.   

This procurement has been carried out by NHS South, Central and West Commissioning Support Unit (SCW) on behalf of the Commissioner(s).

title: SC22302 - AE670 (Permissive Bridleway) Surface and Infrastructure Improvements
description:
Kent County Council is seeking to commission a Contractor to deliver surface and infrastructure improvements to a Permissive Bridleway, which is part of the North Downs Way National Trail. The path is located in Brabourne, Ashford.

The surface of the Bridleway has become extremely muddy and significantly worn at regular intervals with a considerable number of potholes developing, and as a result, suffers from large puddles of water forming during periods of sustained rainfall. Frequent pedestrian, cycle and equestrian traffic along this section, as well as being an access route for agricultural vehicles to and from the neighbouring fields, prevent it from recovering and continued use by these groups will cause its condition to deteriorate further and inhibit use from this range of user groups, particularly during winter months.

The North Downs Way (NDW), which has National Trail status, is a popular and heavily used trail through Kent and recognised and lauded for its spectacular views and fascinating heritage, traversing the Kent Downs Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty. By carrying out repairs and improvements to the surface, it will maintain access, allows safe an accessible passage and supports continued and longer-term tourism, as well as sustainable economic, environmental and social benefits. Furthermore, the improvements will facilitate and mitigate the expected increase in the number of people using the route and rural Anti-Social Behaviour, together with significantly reducing further damage to the surface.

title: SC22328 - AE36 (Byway) Surface Repairs
description:
Kent County Council is seeking to commission a Contractor to deliver surface repairs to a Byway, which is part of the North Downs Way National Trail. The path is located in Chilham, Ashford.

In recent years the surface of the Byway has become significantly rutted, with loose flints and stones dispersed throughout, and at sections, the underlying native chalk substrate exposed, a consequence of heavy rainfall and the flow of surface water combined with the gradient of the path.

Frequent pedestrian, cycle and equestrian traffic along this section of the Byway, as well as its current condition prevent it from recovering and continued use by these groups will cause it to deteriorate further and inhibit use from this range of user groups both during dry and wet weather.

The intention is to create a planer path with a slight crossfall to steer and allow surface water to run off the path into adjacent woodland. Where there is woodland or drainage ditches on either side of the path, a cambered surface on the Byway is proposed.

The North Downs Way (NDW), which has National Trail status, is a popular and heavily used trail through Kent and recognised and lauded for its spectacular views and fascinating heritage, traversing the Kent Downs Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty. By carrying out repairs and improvements to the surface, it will maintain access, allows safe an accessible passage and supports continued and longer-term tourism, as well as sustainable economic, environmental and social benefits. Furthermore, the improvements will facilitate and mitigate the expected increase in the number of people using the route and rural Anti-Social Behaviour, together with significantly reducing further damage to the surface.

The Experience project supports the development and delivery of sustainable projects that enable the improvement and enjoyment of the Kent countryside, particularly those which can be promoted and used by the local community and visitors during the winter months (October to March, referred to as the 'off season').

The Experience project focuses on outdoor tourism activities and opportunities which actively encourage and attract walkers, cyclists and equestrians to the Kent countryside, as well as promoting active travel and supporting the local economy. The East Kent Public Rights of Way (PROW) Team has a particular remit to improve the routes along the Cycling UK East Kent Riders Route, as well as the renowned National Trail, the North Downs Way, both of which this Byway is part of.

Through the Experience Project funding, the East Kent PROW team have a dedicated project budget to support and proactively deliver infrastructure improvement projects that mutually contribute to and achieve these outcomes.
There is a requirement for prompt delivery and completion, as the Experience Project concludes at the end of March 2023, by which time the funding allocated to support these improvement works must be spent.
